name: ITI Wireman
title: ITI Wireman
intro: The ITI Wireman roadmap: eligibility, admission, trade training, the All India Trade Test, apprenticeship and jobs, in order.

phases.title: Eligibility after Class 8 or 10
phases.summary: Eligibility for this trade: Class 10 pass (check the state rule).
points: ITI admission needs a minimum age of 14 years and the Class 8 or Class 10 pass level fixed for the trade; check the exact requirement on your state’s ITI admission portal.
Science and Maths in school help for technical trades, but you can still join if the trade allows it.
Choose the trade by interest and local job demand; talk to ITI instructors and working technicians.
Government ITIs have limited seats and low fees; private ITIs must be affiliated to NCVT, so verify affiliation on the DGT site.

phases.title: ITI admission process
phases.summary: Online application on the state ITI portal, merit list and counselling.
points: Register on your state’s ITI admission portal (or the DGT portal where used), enter marks, upload documents and pay the application fee.
Seats are allotted through merit lists and counselling rounds; select trade and ITI preferences carefully.
Reserved-category seats and women’s and PwD quotas apply as per state rules.
Report to the allotted ITI with originals, pay fees and complete admission before the cut-off date.
facts: Online application → merit list → counselling → admission
phases.tip: Many states hold several rounds; keep checking the portal even if you miss your first choice.

phases.title: Trade theory and practical training
phases.summary: Learn the fundamentals: wiring of houses and buildings, conduit and cable laying, earthing, switchgear, meters, and testing and fault finding.
points: Trade practical: wiring of houses and buildings, conduit and cable laying, earthing, switchgear, meters, and testing and fault finding.
Tools and equipment you will use: wire strippers, pliers, testers, multimeter, drills and cable tools.
Trade theory, workshop calculation and science, engineering drawing and employability skills (communication, entrepreneurship) are taught alongside practicals.
Learn safe isolation, earthing and protective devices; electrical accidents are preventable with the right procedure.
facts: wire strippers, pliers, testers, multimeter, drills and cable tools

phases.title: Advanced training, projects and CITS
phases.summary: Deeper skills and, for two-year trades, advanced practice.
points: Two-year trades add advanced trade practicals, projects and more detailed theory in the second year; one-year trades complete these topics in a compressed form.
You may do industrial visits and on-the-job exposure organised by the ITI.
Keep a record of your practicals and projects; assessors check them in the trade test.
ITI instructors and many employers also value the Craft Instructor Training Scheme (CITS) if you later want to teach in an ITI.

phases.title: All India Trade Test and NCVT certificate
phases.summary: AITT is the national exam that gives the National Trade Certificate (NTC).
points: The All India Trade Test (AITT) is conducted by the Directorate General of Training (DGT) under NCVT, covering trade theory, trade practical, workshop calculation and science, engineering drawing and employability skills.
Passing it gives you the National Trade Certificate (NTC), which is recognised across India.
Keep your NTC, marksheets and trainee registration number safe; employers and apprenticeship portals ask for them.
Many states also run internal assessments; follow your ITI’s timetable for exam forms.

phases.title: Apprenticeship and job entry
phases.summary: Wireman apprentices are taken by electrical contractors, building firms and distribution companies.
points: After ITI you can register on the Apprenticeship India portal and apply to companies for a one-year apprenticeship under the Apprentices Act; you earn a stipend while training.
Completing an apprenticeship gives the National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC), which improves job prospects and is accepted for many government recruitments.
Typical jobs: wireman, electrical helper, panel assembler and maintenance assistant.
Self-employment: house wiring and repair work, subject to local electrical licensing rules.

phases.title: Licensing, upgrading and government jobs
phases.summary: Add a licence, a diploma or government recruitment to grow.
points: A wireman or contractor licence from your state’s Electrical Licensing Board is needed for independent electrical contracting; check the exam and experience requirements in your state.
Upgrade: join the ITI Electrician trade or a diploma through lateral entry, where eligible.
Government and PSU recruitment: Indian Railways (RRB Technician, Group D and ALP posts), defence establishments, PSUs and state departments regularly recruit ITI holders for relevant trades.
Short upskilling courses under Skill India and employer training improve your pay and role.
